- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% lag correction to forecast.
- Sentiment spikes correlate with forecast bias: if sentiment rises >0.2 for 3+ days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% per sentiment unit.
